integrity: The proof is a finite-incidence double count in \(\operatorname{PG}(4,2)\). It separately accounts for equal, intersecting, and skew pairs of line copies, so multiplicities are not silently discarded. A standalone verifier reconstructs the complete projective incidence geometry and checks an explicit \(32\)-line lower-bound witness.
scientific_limitations: The exact value remains \(32\) or \(33\); existence of a \(33\)-line configuration is not decided. The lower bound \(32\) is prior work. Novelty is restricted to the theoretical upper bound \(33\) and the rigidity of a hypothetical \(33\)-line extremizer.
title: A theoretical \(33\)-line ceiling for the first unresolved binary plane-cap parameter
